description: Two RV32I cores designed from the specification, verified against an independent reference, with the workflow's own detection power measured by mutation testing.

criteria.criterion: every encoder output matches the official machine-readable tables
no base RV32I instruction is missing from the encoder
every RV32I instruction is executed by the corpus
every declared corner bin is reached by the corpus
the whole corpus agrees exactly with the independent reference
a mutation campaign has been run and its score reported
criteria.note: Run with workspace/rv32i/reference/mutation.py. It rebuilds the RTL per mutant and is too slow for every verification pass; results are recorded in workspace/rv32i/docs/WORKFLOW.md.

criteria.criterion: every surviving mutant is classified as a stimulus gap or an equivalent mutant
each equivalence claim is supported by measurement, not by argument alone
criteria.note: The pipeline equivalence claim is additionally encoded as a runtime assertion, so it is re-checked on every run.

criteria.criterion: results are confirmed against an implementation this repository did not write
criteria.note: Two independent oracles. CV32E40P is an unmodified silicon-proven core, authoritative for every rule its ISA shares with this one. The Sail model is the executable specification itself, configured to the exact ISA under test, and is authoritative where they differ.

criteria.criterion: any ground truth that could not be run is recorded as unavailable with its reason
criteria.note: riscv-arch-test remains unavailable: its test setup requires Zicsr and M-mode CSRs that this core does not implement. Recorded as unavailable, never as passed.

criteria.criterion: per-instruction semantics are proven, not sampled
criteria.note: riscv-formal bounded model checking with SymbiYosys and z3. Proves no counterexample exists within each check's depth; not an unbounded proof.
